question.problem:
Consider the differential equation 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=3-\frac{1}{(3x-y)^{3}}.
$$

Using a substitution of the form $z=3x-y,$ transform the differential equation into an equation of the form ${z}^{′}(x)=f(z).$ What is the function $f(z)?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we make the substitution

$$
z=3x-y.
$$

Differentiating $z(x)$ using the chain rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}=3-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=3-\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Therefore, the original equation can be written in terms of $z$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3-\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =3-\frac{1}{{z}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing this equation in the form ${z}^{′}(x)=f(z),$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{{z}^{3}}.
$$

Therefore, $f(z)=\frac{1}{{z}^{3}}.$
